stem: Which Salter-Harris fracture types are associated with higher rates of physeal arrest (growth cessation)?
explanation: These types involve the epiphysis or direct crushing of the plate, which significantly increases the risk of growth complications.
rationale: Focus on the higher-numbered classifications that involve the joint or compression.

optionExplanations.A: These types involve the epiphysis or direct crushing of the plate, which significantly increases the risk of growth complications.
optionExplanations.B: Types I and II generally have a lower risk of growth arrest because they do not involve the germinal layer or epiphysial blood supply as directly.
optionExplanations.C: While Type III has risks, Type II is generally considered lower risk for growth arrest compared to Types IV and V.
optionExplanations.D: While Type V has a high risk, Types III and IV also carry significant risks due to their intraarticular and trans-physeal nature.

source.hint: Focus on the higher-numbered classifications that involve the joint or compression.
